name: Breadcrumb Intent
summary: UX vocabulary for a location trail: an ordered path from a root section to the current page, where earlier items are links back up and the last item is the current page. Refines the hierarchical structure of the Navigation intent (the current-item marker is derived from it) and composes the Typography intent for responsible label truncation. The block contract is src/_data/blocks/breadcrumb.json.

current.description: How the last item is presented. It is always the current page: a plain non-link node marked aria-current="page" (derived from Navigation hierarchical structure). This is a closed enum: accessibility-load-bearing, never extended.

separator.description: How items are divided. Presentational only (CSS or aria-hidden), never an announced character. This is a closed enum: accessibility-load-bearing, never extended.

overflow.description: What happens when the trail is wider than its container: leading ancestors collapse behind one disclosure (an ellipsis item that reveals them in place), keeping the immediate parent and the current item visible. Never wrap or scroll. This is a closed enum.

description:
The Breadcrumb Intent describes where the user is within a hierarchy. It composes the Navigation intent (structure: hierarchical) and the Typography intent, and adds only the trail presentation.

Landmark

The trail sits in a nav landmark with an accessible name, and the items form an ordered list. A single-item trail adds nothing and renders nothing.

Current Item

The last item is the current page: aria-current="page", not a link. Every earlier item is a link.

Separator

A divider hidden from assistive technology so the trail reads as an ordered list, never as announced characters.

Overflow

collapse: leading ancestors fold into one disclosure that expands the full trail in place; the immediate parent and the current item stay visible. Only as a last resort is the current item's label truncated, and that truncation follows the Typography intent's truncation paradigm: the full text stays in the DOM and is recoverable (expand or title), never lost.
